entry.title: Western Startups Realigning Chinese AI Models for Western Markets
entry.content:
Links: restofworld.org

Western startups including Hirundo and Lazarus AI are modifying open-weight artificial intelligence models from Chinese developers such as DeepSeek and Alibaba to remove state-aligned censorship, fix code vulnerabilities, and meet Western corporate standards. These firms use machine unlearning and weight-editing techniques to adapt the models for enterprises that want to leverage high-performance, low-cost Chinese technology without perceived security risks.

While these interventions have enabled deployment across dozens of U.S. companies, some government agencies remain reluctant to adopt Chinese models regardless of modification. Meanwhile, AI researchers note that universal alignment remains an elusive standard, while many commercial developers continue to use unedited Chinese models without encountering practical restrictions.

entry.title: Researchers Introduce Weight-Space Programming for Direct Neural Network Weight Manipulation
entry.content:
Links: rikiyat.github.io | hacker news

Researchers have introduced weight-space programming, a paradigm where frontier large language models like GPT-6 Astra natively read and write neural network weights without relying on traditional gradient-descent optimizers. By reasoning directly over raw weight matrices, the model can identify trained tasks, generate small game-playing networks from scratch, and pinpoint structural flaws in existing architectures.

In evaluations, Astra corrected reasoning loops in Qwen3.5-0.8B by modifying just 0.016% of its weights, raising its math benchmark performance from 7.9% to 48.1% while improving instruction following. This approach replaces conventional symbolic optimization with reasoning-driven modifications, pointing toward new methods for model interpretability and self-correction.

entry.title: SemiAnalysis Launches GDPx Benchmark for Frontier AI Models
entry.content:
Links: newsletter.semianalysis.com

SemiAnalysis has introduced GDPx, a benchmark designed to evaluate general agentic capabilities across high-value domains such as chip design, cybersecurity, biology, finance, and software engineering. Unlike broader economic benchmarks that include sectors less reliant on frontier intelligence, GDPx focuses specifically on fields where advanced AI models are expected to have the highest economic impact.

Developed in partnership with specialized reinforcement learning environment startups, GDPx incorporates complex, multi-file simulated environments and rigorous quality assurance protocols to avoid the limitations of older static benchmarks like GDPval. Initial evaluations show that even leading frontier models score roughly 12% overall, highlighting significant performance variations and the impact of built-in safety classifiers across different domains.

entry.title: India's Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology Unveils DEPA Framework for AI Training
entry.content:
Links: theregister.com | meity.gov.in

India's Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology has released a handbook on the Data Empowerment and Protection Architecture for AI Training framework. The initiative allows AI models to travel to decentralized data sources rather than requiring raw data to be transferred to model developers, utilizing hardware-based secure environments to maintain privacy and security.

The framework aims to unlock fragmented sectors like healthcare, financial services, and education for local artificial intelligence development while keeping data owners in control and preventing big tech dominance. It forms part of India's broader push for digital public infrastructure and aims to serve as a model for global science diplomacy and responsible AI governance.

entry.title: Memdoor Releases Team-Solve Workflow Implementing GVS5H Multi-Agent Architecture
entry.content:
Links: github.com | hacker news

Memdoor has published a new workflow implementation called team-solve, based on the GVS5H training-free self-orchestration method. The architecture coordinates five distinct Qwen3.8-27B agent instances—acting as a planner, two ideators, a solver, a manager, and a repair worker—running with fresh contexts and communicating solely through files on disk rather than shared memory or chat windows.

Tested on the first ten problems of the LiveCodeBench Hard benchmark across five passes, the file-based multi-agent setup achieved a mean score of 9.8 out of 10, matching the performance of the authors' original research harness. Each run took a median of 40 minutes at a cost of approximately $0.39, utilizing eight YAML configuration files without custom code or hardcoded model names.

entry.title: OpenAI, Google, Microsoft, and Anthropic to Adopt Shared AI Scraping Opt-Out Standard
entry.content:
Links: theverge.com

A new standard proposed through the Internet Engineering Task Force (IETF) will allow web publishers to opt out of AI training using a single signal in their robots.txt files. OpenAI, Google, Microsoft, and Anthropic have announced they will adopt this shared "policy token," which enables website owners to communicate scraping preferences to multiple AI providers simultaneously rather than managing individual settings for each company.

Anthropic has already adopted the signal, while OpenAI plans to implement it in the coming months. Google and Microsoft expect to support the standard next year, with Microsoft indicating it will provide granular controls for distinguishing between AI training and AI grounding. Meta has expressed support for the standard but has not yet committed to an implementation timeline.

The experiment highlights how autonomous LLM swarms can develop complex social protocols and risk aversion when faced with survival pressures.

Altman also addresses the safety challenges of sandboxing superhuman models and the architectural shifts required as personal agents transform software development.

He emphasizes the importance of iterative deployment and practical empowerment over rigid safety narratives, arguing that AI systems must provide tangible benefits and individual freedom rather than fostering a restrictive surveillance state.

entry.title: Claude Code Background Agent Summaries Consuming 20 Percent of Tokens Addressed by Bun Preload
entry.content:
Links: gist.github.com | hacker news

Claude Code periodically sends the full transcripts of background agents to their respective models every 30 seconds to generate brief status descriptions, a process that accounts for 15 to 20 percent of total token consumption. This background activity occurs without user configuration options to disable it, impacting rate-limit headroom primarily through automated model requests that do not contribute to the main conversation.

To eliminate this overhead, developers have created a Bun preload script that intercepts and suppresses the specific timers responsible for triggering the summary requests. Testing across multiple versions indicates that disabling the feature successfully eliminates these requests while maintaining normal operation for background agents and subagents.

entry.title: Qwenputer Embeds RISC-V CPU into Qwen 3.5 Weights
entry.content:
Links: divagr.com | github.com | hacker news

Qwenputer is an experimental model based on Qwen 3.5 4B that embeds a 32-bit RISC-V CPU directly into its weights. By using Gated DeltaNet (GDN) layers as exact, addressable RAM, the CPU executes arithmetic, C, and MicroPython code during forward passes without external runtimes or tool calls.

The implementation uses one-hot key encoding for memory access and has achieved 100% accuracy on specific long-integer arithmetic benchmarks. An experimental filesystem also allows the model to store and retrieve text data via the DeltaNet state, providing persistent memory across conversation sessions.
